ei.title: Chapter 0-QN23~24 1번: Market Incentives and Ecosystem Services
ei.subject: 올림포스9대변별유형

fullPassage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that provide financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to favor ecosystem services over extractive uses.

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that (A)[provide / withhold] financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than (B)[manage / neglect] the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may (C)[exceed / reduce] the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to favor ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 재정적 보상을 제공하다, 숲을 관리하다, 목재의 가치를 초과하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① withhold — manage — exceed (A 반대: 제공하다→보류하다)
✅ ② provide — manage — exceed — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ provide — neglect — exceed (B 반대: 관리하다→방치하다)
❌ ④ provide — manage — reduce (C 반대: 초과하다→줄이다)

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that provide financial rewards for (A)[exploitation / preservation]. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to (B)[influence / obstruct] management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to (C)[favor / oppose] ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 착취에 대한 보상, 관리 결정에 영향을 미치다, 생태계 서비스를 선호하다
det.analysis:
✅ ① exploitation — influence — favor — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② preservation — influence — favor (A 반대: 착취→보존)
❌ ③ exploitation — obstruct — favor (B 반대: 영향을 미치다→방해하다)
❌ ④ exploitation — influence — oppose (C 반대: 선호하다→반대하다)

For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times (B)[greater / smaller] per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically (C)[inefficient / profitable], and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to favor ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 재정적 보상, 세 배 더 큰 이익, 경제적으로 비효율적인
det.analysis:
❌ ① emotional — greater — inefficient (A 반대: 재정적인→감정적인)
❌ ② financial — smaller — inefficient (B 반대: 더 큰→더 작은)
✅ ③ financial — greater — inefficient — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ financial — greater — profitable (C 반대: 비효율적인→수익성 있는)

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that ①<u>provide</u> financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than ②<u>exploit</u> the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including ③<u>climate</u> regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to ④<u>favor</u> ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① provide(제공하다) ✅ / ② exploit(착취하다) ❌ → manage(관리하다) / ③ climate(기후) ✅ / ④ favor(선호하다) ✅
det.analysis:
① provide(제공하다): 시장 유인이 재정적 보상을 제공한다 — 적절 ✅
② exploit(착취하다): 원문은 manage(관리하다). 나무를 베는 것과 대조되는 것은 숲을 '관리'하는 것이지 '착취'가 아님 ←정답
③ climate(기후): 기후 조절은 생태계 서비스의 예 — 적절 ✅
④ favor(선호하다): 시장이 생태계 서비스를 선호하도록 신호를 보내야 함 — 적절 ✅
det.tip: manage(관리하다) ↔ exploit(착취하다). 벌목의 대안은 숲을 '관리'하는 것

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that provide financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market ①<u>incentive</u> to cut down trees rather than manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to ②<u>influence</u> management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water ③<u>pollution</u>, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically ④<u>inefficient</u>, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to favor ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① incentive(유인) ✅ / ② influence(영향을 미치다) ✅ / ③ pollution(오염) ❌ → purification(정화) / ④ inefficient(비효율적인) ✅
det.analysis:
① incentive(유인): 숲 주인에게 나무를 벨 시장 유인이 있음 — 적절 ✅
② influence(영향을 미치다): 재정적 이익이 없어 관리 결정에 영향을 미치기 어려움 — 적절 ✅
③ pollution(오염): 원문은 purification(정화). 생태계 서비스로 열거된 것은 물 '정화'이지 물 '오염'이 아님 ←정답
④ inefficient(비효율적인): 나무를 베는 것은 경제적으로 비효율적임 — 적절 ✅

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources ①<u>rarely</u> face market incentives that provide financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife ②<u>habitat</u>, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may ③<u>exceed</u> the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to favor ecosystem services over ④<u>extractive</u> uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① rarely(드물게) ❌ → typically(일반적으로) / ② habitat(서식지) ✅ / ③ exceed(초과하다) ✅ / ④ extractive(채굴의) ✅
det.analysis:
① rarely(드물게): 원문은 typically(일반적으로). 글 전체가 관리자들이 '일반적으로' 착취를 보상하는 유인에 직면한다는 전제에서 출발하므로 '드물게'는 논지 모순 ←정답
② habitat(서식지): 야생동물 서식지는 생태계 서비스 — 적절 ✅
③ exceed(초과하다): 비시장 가치의 경제적 이익이 목재 가치를 초과할 수 있음 — 적절 ✅
④ extractive(채굴의): 생태계 서비스와 대비되는 채굴적 이용 — 적절 ✅
det.tip: typically(일반적으로) ↔ rarely(드물게). 글의 대전제와 일치해야 함

questions.passage:
(A) Managers of natural resources typically <u>face</u> market incentives that reward the exploitation of forests.

(B) She could not hide the shock on her <u>face</u> when she heard the terrible news about the flood.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 face의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) face = 직면하다, 마주하다 (동사) / (B) face = 얼굴 (명사)
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 직면하다 — (B) 얼굴: (A)는 유인에 '직면하다', (B)는 그녀의 '얼굴'에 드러난 충격 ←정답
❌ ② (A) 얼굴 — (B) 직면하다: 두 문맥의 의미가 서로 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ (A) 표면 — (B) 체면: (A)는 표면이 아닌 직면, (B)는 체면이 아닌 얼굴
❌ ④ (A) 향하다 — (B) 표정: (A)는 단순히 향하는 것이 아니라 직면하는 것
det.tip: face: 직면하다(v.) / 얼굴(n.) / 표면(n.) — 문맥으로 품사와 의미 판단

det.korean: 동물이나 식물이 정상적으로 사는 자연적 환경 = habitat(서식지)
det.analysis:
❌ ① incentive(유인): 행동을 부추기는 요인이지 서식지 아님
❌ ② resource(자원): 이용 대상이지 사는 환경 아님
❌ ③ initiative(계획): 계획이지 환경 아님
✅ ④ habitat(서식지): 동식물이 사는 자연 환경 — 정의 일치 ←정답
det.tip: habitat = 서식지 (the natural home of an animal or plant)

questions.passage: For example, a United Nations initiative has __________ (estimate) that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: estimate(추정하다) → estimated (현재완료 has estimated)
det.analysis: 조동사 has 뒤에는 과거분사가 와야 함. estimate → estimated. 'has estimated' = (지금까지) 추정해 왔다. 주어는 a United Nations initiative.

questions.passage: The economic benefits of ecosystem services include climate regulation, water purification, and erosion __________ (prevent). These non-market benefits may exceed the economic value of the timber.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: prevent(막다) → prevention (명사: 예방, 방지)
det.analysis: climate regulation, water purification, erosion ___ 은 명사구의 병렬 구조. 앞의 regulation·purification과 짝을 이루는 명사가 필요하므로 prevent → prevention. 'erosion prevention' = 침식 방지.
det.tip: prevent(v.) → prevention(n. 예방, 방지). 명사 병렬 구조

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that provide __________ for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to favor ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 시장 유인은 착취에 대한 재정적 보상을 제공한다
det.analysis:
❌ ① legal penalties(법적 처벌): 유인은 처벌이 아니라 보상
❌ ② moral obligations(도덕적 의무): 시장 유인의 성격과 무관
✅ ③ financial rewards(재정적 보상): 시장 유인이 자원 착취에 재정적 보상을 제공 — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ physical barriers(물리적 장벽): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: market incentive = 시장의 재정적 보상 (financial rewards)

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that provide financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their __________, may exceed the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to favor ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 비시장 가치에 근거한 경제적 이익이 목재의 경제적 가치를 초과할 수 있다
det.analysis:
✅ ① non-market values(비시장 가치): 시장에서 거래되지 않는 생태계 서비스의 가치 — 뒤의 '시장 이익'과 대비 — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② market prices(시장 가격): 생태계 서비스는 시장 가격이 매겨지지 않음
❌ ③ legal restrictions(법적 제한): 이익 산정의 근거가 아님
❌ ④ physical limits(물리적 한계): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: non-market values = 비시장 가치 (시장에서 거래되지 않는 생태계의 가치)
